CAMP BIRECTOR’S REPORT 


INTRODUCTION: 


Well 1979 has come to an end and we made it. We managed to survive two 
severe rainstorms, a problem with our septic system, problems with our 
van and trailer and a 10% returnee staff. It's my hope that. this report 
will be a guide for next year in the areas of staff training, program, 
equipment, site and facility improvements. 


| feel very optimistic about the future of Kanawana and its positive 
effect on children and staff. 


KAMPERS : 


This summer we worked with 441 different kampers and 18 C.I|.T.s. Kanawana 
accepted children from Youth Horizons, Children's Mountain Cottage and 
some sponsored by the Rotary Club of Westmount. 


Our total number of kamper weeks including C.!.T.s was 1,375. This 
figure includes 132 weeks for the C.I.T.s. Our returnee rate was 48.80% 
which is down 7.31% from the overall returnee rate of last year. 


STAFF: 


Staff hiring commenced the second week of April and we were still hiring 
in key positions six days into pre-kamp. Faced .with a 10% returnee rate 
from last year, interviewing and finding staff became a major concern. 
In the end | was very pleased overall! with the staff and their desire to 
do a good job. Their dedication and concern has influenced and enriched 
many who participated in Kanawana '79. 


The organization and supervision of the Sections, Hike ahd Trip, Arts and 
Crafts, Waterfront and Business Office were handled by a senior staff team. 
Their maturity and sensitivity made them most effective in their work. |} 
sincerely thank them for their consistent support, dedication and co- 
operation throughout the summer. 


Kevin Forster was the Assistant Kamp Director and deserves special mention. 
Many of the supervisory roles and programs of the kamp were well handled 
and organized under Kevin's excellent direction. | thank him for his 
support and for being an integral part of Kanawana 1979.

PRE-KAMP 


STAFF TRAINING: 
Staff training started in June this year with a compulsory First-Aid course 
for those who didn't possess a valid certificate at the time. This should 
continue next year. This was then followed by a 9 day pre-kamp which Kevin 
Forster and other returning staff designed and developed. Pre-kamp was 
very successful but there are a few recommendations to be considered next 
year. 

- More waterfront time - at least 10 hours. 


- Canoeing and Sailing - more time and preparation and work on 
canoes and sailboats. 


- Pre-kamp should be more skill oriented ie canoeing, sailing 
and campcraft. 


- Reduce amount of time spent on naturelore. 
- Staff should choose interest groups before pre-kamp. 


- Short canoe trip - at least with trippers if not entire 
staff (2-3 days out of kamp). 


- Leadership style be reduced to 1/2 day at most, possibly 
get to know you games more beneficial. 


- Continue First-Aid. 
- In-town sessions before kamp should include program 
resourcesfulness, teaching methodology, rainy day 


programs (first session 7 days of rain). 


- Astronomy, campfire program and naturelore incorporated 
into canoe trip. 


- Promote Hebertism and Orienteering. 


- Promote use of entire site at Kamp Kanawana instead of 
immediate core. 


- Let's concentrate on those basic skills. 
Also, it's important that staff be sent on courses. Two staff persons 


were sent to the Ontario Woodsmanship School and one staff person to 
a Rock Climbing course. 


Staff Training Cont'd 
Next year send trippers to Woodsmanship Schoo! and some to Canoe School. 


Somebody should be sent to Archery, Astronomy, Naturelore or Environmental 
School, Hebertism and Sailing. 


| feel pre-kamp ended with good group cohesiveness and the tone being set 
for the summer. 


Pre-Pre-Kamp: 


Get people involved earlier in planning pre-kamp in town. Give them the 
time before pre-kamp to plan sessions properly and to get to know each 
other more, Involve all senior staff and some of returning staff. This 
+ime was used for senior staff to get priorities and objectives set and 
also for the planning of pre-kamp. | feel that this should be separated 
somewhat next year. Extend the total to 5 days - 2 for senior staff 
orientation and 3 for pre-kamp planning. 


PROGRAM: 


Interest Groups: 


Overall interest groups were run well but for next year we should decide 
early what interest group counsellors are interested in instructing so 
that research may be done in the area and we can expect higher qual ity 
of instruction with more enthusiasm and alternatives in methodology of 
instruction. \ 


Program Areas - Recommendations: 


Canoeing - A Director for specifically canoeing program and the program 
should have more qualified diligent instructors. 


New streaming in the C-B-A levels (size and age) 
Consider free boating for practice. 


"B" Canoeing suffered - no qualified instructor 
really, other than David. 


Repairs on equipment started earlier. 
Paddles lost through use and abuse, replaced. 
Sailing - One Director for this area also. 


Follow National YMCA program. 


Sailing Cont'd 
Instructors should know ahead of time what level they'l| 
be teaching in order to concentrate their skills to that 
level. 
Improve storage of sails and other equipment. 
Sailing dock moved to deep water. 
Padding on wood frame about cement. 
Repair all boats before the summer. 

Rowboating-Improve storage and mooring. 
Some boats in need of repair. 
How about a glass bottom rowboat? 

Swimming - Lifeguarding very good. 
Change boom to inside of outer docks. 


More emphasis on getting down to waterfront on time 
for lifeguarding duties. 


During change-over go over search and rescue procedure. 


10 hours needed in pre-kamp - lifesaving, search and 
stroke improvement. 


Guycan useless need a better storage area. 
Campcraft - Lesson plans should be given out during pre-kamp. 
Rock Climbing - Equipment too limited if want to expand program. 
Sports Fitness - Too much floor hockey and running. If Katimivik 

to be used pillars to be padded. 

Not a Phys Ed class, more fun. 


Think about separating girls from guys re activities. 


Arts & Crafts - Program very good, we should still try to get more 
into crafts for seniors. 


List of equipment purchases at beginning of the year. 
An Assistant to help with large tent groups. 


Tools need sharpening. 


Naturelore - A specialist who could concentrate on program would help. 


More supervision on water areas. 


Buy equipment for program eg aquariums and books. 


Orienteering- Kids not interested in it but maybe change emphasis. 


Archery - 


Dance - 


Drama - 


Should be integral part of overall program. 

Staff and campers should experience a competition. 
Need a qualified instructor. 

Buy a good bow. 

Motivation. 


Another haystack would allow several tent groups use 
area in afternoon. 


Cut underbrush behind to limit lost arrows. 
More international and folk dance. 

Get records and equipment before start of kamp. 
Good program for all ages. 

More flexibility in types of drama. 


Less formal, Kabaret type lots more fun. 


Some areas to look at next year: 


All-Kamp - 


Hebertism course 
Work projects for C.I|.T.s 


Senior boys more contributions to the kamp, 
especially for those who have been at kamp 
for number of years. 


The majority of All-Kamps were successful. | feel that 
the atmosphere should de-emphasize competition and be 
more of a fun activity. All-Kamps are important in that 
they give the campers an opportunity to take a break 
from the schedule and participate as an entire kamp. 

lt enhances more interaction within kamp. 


Section Programs - More emphasis on this area re campfires, 
sing songs and games. 


Hike & Trip - There was a definite improvement in inventory control 
and the equipment purchased at the beginning of the 
year added to the quality of program. 


Better examination of canoes on return and repairs 
carried out immediately. 


Try to schedule more trips by assigning more counsel lors 
trippers' positions in senior boys and girls. 


Schedule days off so they coincide with change-over. 


All Hike & Trip staff should stagger days off so that 
there is always someone around to give out Hike and 
Trip information. 


Buy new tripping packs for next year. 

Let's get back to Gumperts, gibbons quality is poor. 
Calendar of trips be set up at beginning of summer. 
Extended trip for 6-8 week campers. 

Trippers take out extended trips. 


C.1.T. Program - This summer we started with 18 Counsel lors-in- 
Training and we finished up with 15. Sarah Scowan became 
a counsellor and two C.|.T.s were dismissed because of 
unacceptable behaviour. There were no other problems 
encountered this year and | feel that the program was a 
positive and rewarding experience for all those involved. 


There are a number of C.I|.T.s that should be considered 
for positions next year and because of age restrictions 
some taken on as junior counsellors or second staff 
positions (auxiliary roles). 


| feel there should be a model designed which would 
accommodate (15-16) - (16-17) year olds. Possibly a 2 year 
program, first year theory and some practical, second year 
junior counsellor or an auxiliary position. 


HEALTH & SAFETY: 
This summer we were fortunate to have a great infirmary team of Dr. Bob 
Bluman, Nurse Therese Marin and Assistant Nurse Janice Evans. They 
always gave excellent care and participated in the kamp whenever possible. 
In general health at kamp was very good especially after talking to other 
camp directors. Our main concerns seemed to be one day flus, colds, ear 
aches, small cuts and scrapes and wasp stings. My only recommendation 
for next year is that there be more follow up with parents whose children 
may have anything that could cause serious concern. A personal telephone 
call from the Doctor or myself goes a long way in re-assuring parents and 
in the final result makes our job easier. 
MAINTENANCE: 
Julian is fantastic what can one say, without his support and never ending 
energy this summer would not have been as personally rewarding as it was. 
Julian is a man with a problem who comes to you with solutions. Above and 
beyond the normal maintenance and repairs he managed to find time to work 
on the following: 

- The septic system 

- The construction of new stairs to the dining hall. 

- Painting the inside of the Business Office. 

- Finishing the interiors of 3 staff cabins. 

- Straightening cabins and making tent platforms. 

- Expanding the waterfront. 

- Repair to rowboats. 


- Repairing the erosion caused by two severe rainstorms this summer. 


- Repairing erosion caused by the laying of pipes to the septic 
field. 


- Fixing the roofs of the cabooses. 
- Removing the interior of the old walk-in fridge for a new one. 
- The clearing of most sections of shrubbery. 


- And many other things too vast and varied to mention. 
MERCI BIEN!! 


Thank you Julian!! 


In terms of 1980 there are a number of things that require attention. 
SITE_|IMPROVEMENTS : 
- New septic field* 


- Road should be paved to large tree in Girls Section 
far side of waterfront too much erosion during rain. 


- Shower in centre of kamp* 
5 - 6 showers on each side - close down other showers. 
Floors under showers rotten 

- Improve drainage in girls section. 


- Girls toilet facilities to be fixed* 


- We need an artisian well. Present filter system on verge 
of breakdown and total repair* 


- Both sides of Dining Hall stairs should be re-painted. 
- Hospital gallery rotten - needs to be changed. 

- Rotten trim on pioneer cabins and Lighthouse. 

- Pioneer cabins need to be patched. 

- Lighthouse needs repair - rot in areas. 

- Southwind needs to be finished inside. 


- Grande Portage needs to be finished inside - 
wood already purchased. 


- Kitchen boys cabin floor should be fixed. 
- Northern Wind should be painted inside. 

- Need for work on kitchen. 

- Change waterfront slightly - 


Rafts outside boom 


Light in swimming area 
- Cabooses need to be painted (Fall or Spring) 


SITE IMPROVEMENT CONT'D: 


Kitchen 
Pots and pans must be in good condition. 


Tables and counters must be of hard material, non-absorbent, 
easy to wash and disinfect. 


Utensils which are hard to wash and disinfect must be replaced. 


Lighting must be increased re intensity and source at the food 
preparation level. 


To eliminate odor and heat an efficient ventilation system 
with a filter is required.* 


PROMOTION: 


This year's promotion included the fol lowing: 


2300 brochures were distributed via phone inquiries, YMCA Branches 
and staff. 


Brochures and registrations were mailed to all former kampers 
(1978 and 1977). 


Several advertisements for Kanawana were placed in the following 
newspapers: 


Gazette Montreal Star 
News & Chronicle Le Dimanche-Matin 
Le Mirabel The Suburban 
Town of Mount Royal Westmount Examiner 
Week Post 
Two issues of the Green Triangle were sent to all 1978 Kanawanians. 
The Kamp Kanawana birthday card was sent out to all '78 kampers. 


Feature articles appeared in the News & Chronicle and the Town of 
Mount “Royal Weekly Post. 


Kanawana was listed in the Quebec Camping Association Directory of 
Accredited Camps. 


The Kanawana reunion was held in April at the Westmount YMCA. 
Two new designs were printed on the T-shirts for Kanawana this 


summer and were enthusiastically received by the kampers and 
staff.

FOOD SERVICES: 


| was not satisfied this year with the services offered by Fan Fare 
Foods Limited. Overall the service can only be rated as average. In 
past years the previous Director and staff were very satisfied . This 
year. the quality, quantity and variety often came into question by 
kampers, staff and parents. 


When we look at our statistics from post-kamp questionnaires we find 
that parents rated the food fairly closely to our 1976 statistics. 
That was our last year of being involved with the total kitchen 
operation. With this in mind, consideration should be made into an 
alternate means of service. 


Here are the results of our post-kamp questionnaires to parents rating 
the food

MONTREAL OFFICE: 


Well, I, don't think Olga has had a busier year than this,a new Director, 
a new staff and very little time to get things done. It was done though 
and Olga managed to be efficient as always and, of course, pleasant. 


| was always amazed at what a resource Olga is without her patience and 
experience | would have been at a loss. Thanks beautiful lady. 


Also, special thanks to Helene Nollet for her assistance and support. 
SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS: 


- This year | limited use of the Farmhouse and surrounding buildings 
because | felt that the site was taxed enough with just camp use. 
| feel this should continue next year with the exception of Day Camp 
Wilderness Camp Experience. 


- We should collect a damage deposit from all those who use cabooses 
in the summer in order that they are taken care of and clean when 
the resident leaves. $50.00-$100.00 minimum. 


- Katimivik should be made safer. The beams and rails still need to 
be covered with some protective material. 


- The plastic enclosures tested this year for the dining hall area 
good investment and should have an extended life if properly 
maintained. We should purchase enough for the entire dining hall. 


- We have to spend some time brightening up the dining hall. Its 
quite dark on even the sunniest days. 


- The Voyageur pick-up and drop-offs should somehow coincide with the 
kamp change-over. This would give Kanawana more tripping time. 


- We should have more tripping counsellors to enable us to get a few 
more trips out. 


- The budget should reflect the cost of tripping in a truer sense. 
It is very ambiguous the way it is set up now. 


- |f we are to expand our waterfront facility we must hire more 
qualified and certified staff. 


- We need some flexibility in our sessions to allow a 3 and 5 week 
kamper stay. 


CONCLUSION: 

This being my first year as Director of Kamp Kanawana | must state that 
the rewards have been tremendous. | finished the summer with many fond 
memories of kampers, staff and some ridiculous situations. | feel that 


the success of 1979 is due to the staff and their desire to do a good 
job. 


This was the year of change and may it be a base for years of change to 
come. The success of Kamp Kanawana is due to the influences intrinsic 
and extrinsic to the kamp. Thanks to our Kamp Board, the YMCA and the 
alumni of Kamp Kanawana for their support. 


Thanks to the kampers of '79 who made it happen and being the most 
important part of kamp. Thanks to the senior staff whom | relied on 
for support, patience and direction and to Julian and Olga whose 
experience, understanding and cooperation made my job easy. 


It's my hope that this report will be a useful aid to all those who 
use it next year. 


"Non Nobis Solum! 


G. David Twynam 


Di rector

GOD'S BACK YARD 


Close your eyes and think real hard 
Imagine kamp as God's back yard. 

The grass so green, the hills so tall 
Close your eyes and think of all 

The beauty of our life at kamp, 

The morning sun on the grass so damp. 
Flags in a circle from countries brave 
Close your eyes and see them wave. 


Children together and children apart 

Some grown up and some ready to start. 

Can you picture your cabin or a favorite tree? 
Close your eyes and try to see 

The sounds of night time, dark and still 

The laughter from a far away hill. 

Remember the good times with friends old and new. 
Take all of these memories home with you. 

Yes, we've worked together and played ‘so hard, 

At Kanawana, in God's back yard. 


-..-Joan Dalrymple
